subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

judge.implied_focus: The dominant service aspect (topic) driving each airline review

per_column.name: dominant_topic
per_column.rationale: Directly proposes the review's central aspect (staff, food, seat comfort, etc.), naming the focus concept the analyst should investigate.

per_column.name: review_sentiment
per_column.rationale: Polarity is a coherent facet that pairs with dominant_topic, enabling analysis of which aspect drives positive vs negative reactions.

per_column.name: review_length_category
per_column.rationale: A generic structural/metadata bucket of text length; it does not centre on any review-content aspect and reads as boilerplate noise rather than a facet of the implied focus.

judge.rationale: Two of the three columns cohere around a plausible, data-inferable focus — the dominant service aspect of each review — with sentiment providing a useful cross-cutting facet that turns topic identification into something actionable (which aspects worth analyzing correlate with satisfaction). This is a defensible proposed focus given the vague query. However, review_length_category is a mechanical text-length bucket that dilutes coherence and adds no facet of the content focus, so the set is not tightly centred. The structure is thin: only topic + sentiment genuinely build around the focus, giving a serviceable but underdeveloped predictor/facet set rather than a rich one. The focus itself is non-trivial and investigable, hence moderate actionability, but the grab-bag element and limited depth keep scores middling.
